title: ～ことから — from the fact that ～
summary: States a fact as the basis or origin from which a judgment, name or result arose. Put こと after a plain form and add から. It is rather formal.

patterns.form: 普通形（Nな・Aなだ→な）＋ことから

body.p: A fact leads to a conclusion or judgment: 窓が開いていたことから、泥棒が入ったと分かった. Nouns and な-adjectives take な; い-adjectives and verbs take the plain form, then こと.
Common for the origin of names, for deductions in crime, and in news. It is for objective facts, not personal emotional reasons. More formal than ので or から.

examples.ja: この町（まち）は水（みず）がきれいなことから、有名（ゆうめい）になった。
examples.romaji: Kono machi wa mizu ga kirei na koto kara, yūmei ni natta.
examples.tr: This town became famous because its water is clean.

examples.ja: 窓（まど）が開（あ）いていたことから、泥棒（どろぼう）が入（はい）ったと分（わ）かった。
examples.romaji: Mado ga aite ita koto kara, dorobō ga haitta to wakatta.
examples.tr: From the fact that the window was open, we knew a burglar had gotten in.

examples.ja: 顔（かお）がよく似（に）ていることから、二人（ふたり）は姉妹（しまい）だと思（おも）われた。
examples.romaji: Kao ga yoku nite iru koto kara, futari wa shimai da to omowareta.
examples.tr: Because their faces looked so alike, the two were thought to be sisters.

pitfalls: Do not drop こと. It is for facts as reasons.
It is odd for the speaker's emotion or will: 悲しいことから泣いた sounds unnatural.
